cards.text: Job has lost his children, his wealth and his health (Job 1-2). For chapter after chapter he's argued with his friends (Job 3-31) and asked for a hearing with God (Job 13:3; 23:3-7), and then a young man named Elihu gave a long speech of his own (Job 32-37). Now, finally, after ALL that talking, the LORD Himself answers Job.

cards.question: When the LORD finally answers Job, where does His voice come from?

answers.text: Out of a pillar of cloud

cards.question: The LORD's first words are “Who is this who obscures My counsel by words without knowledge?” He's telling Job that all his talk has made things clearer.

cards.text: Job has wanted to argue his case with God for chapters (Job 13:3; 31:35), and the LORD starts with “Now brace yourself like a man…” Friend, when somebody tells ME to brace myself, I grab the counter with my WHOLE mustache.

cards.question: Now that the LORD is here, He tells Job that He will be the one answering Job's questions.

cards.text: The LORD's first question: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.” And friend, that's just the WARM-UP.

cards.question: The LORD asks who fixed the earth's measurements and who laid its cornerstone. He's talking about the earth like a ___.
When the earth's cornerstone was laid, the morning stars sang together. What were all the sons of God doing?

cards.text: Next, the sea bursts forth from the womb, and the LORD makes the clouds its garment and thick darkness its blanket. A whole OCEAN, friend, and it gets a BLANKET.

cards.question: The sea comes bursting out with its proud waves. What does the LORD do with it?
The LORD speaks right to the sea and tells its proud waves where they must stop.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks if Job, in his days, has ever commanded the morning or assigned the dawn its place, so it spreads to the ends of the earth and shakes the wicked out of it. Friend, most of us lose an argument with the snooze button every single morning.
“The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its hills stand out like the folds of a garment.” Clay under a seal is STAMPING, friend, and that's my whole JOB!
“Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.” Then the LORD's questions head down, WAY down, deeper than the back of the junk drawer I spent years in.

cards.question: Heading down into the depths, where does the LORD ask if Job has journeyed?

answers.text: To the vents of the sea
To the bottom of the Jordan

cards.question: The LORD asks Job whether the gates of death have been revealed to him.

cards.text: The LORD asks if Job has surveyed the extent of the earth. Then He turns to light and darkness.

cards.question: The LORD talks about light and darkness as if each one has a ___ with paths leading to it.
After asking where Job was when He laid the earth's foundations, the LORD tells Job, “Surely you know, for you were already born!” What is He pointing out?

answers.text: Job is older than the earth
Job learned it from his elders

cards.text: Now the LORD asks if Job has entered the storehouses of snow or seen the storehouses of hail. STOREHOUSES, friend. The snow has its own PANTRY.

cards.question: The LORD says He holds the snow and hail in reserve for times of trouble and for the day of war and battle. That means the snow and hail just fall wherever they please.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks which way the lightning is dispersed, and who cuts a channel for the flood and clears a path for the thunderbolt.

cards.question: The LORD says He sends the rain only to places where people live and can use it.

cards.text: Rain on a desert where no man lives, to make the parched wasteland sprout with tender grass. No crowd, no applause, nobody there to say thank you… and He waters it anyway.

cards.question: The LORD asks if the rain has a father and from whose womb the ice comes. What picture is He using for the weather?
The LORD says the surface of the deep never freezes.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to the sky: can Job bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion? Friend, every cookie box I seal lights ONE star over my bakery, and I celebrate like I invented the sky.
He keeps going: can Job bring forth the constellations in their seasons, or lead out the Bear and her cubs?

cards.question: Still looking at the sky, what does the LORD ask if Job knows?

answers.text: The names of all the angels

cards.text: Then the LORD asks if Job can command the clouds so that a flood of water covers him.

cards.question: The LORD asks Job whether the lightning bolts report to him, saying “Here we are”.
The LORD keeps asking Job what he knows and understands. Then, in the middle of the sky and weather questions, He asks where knowing and understanding come from. What does He ask?

answers.text: Who put wisdom in the heart

cards.text: Then the LORD asks who has the wisdom to count the clouds. I spent years counting the dust falling in the junk drawer I was stuck in, friend, and I never once got a final number.

cards.question: The LORD asks who can tilt the water jars of the heavens when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods of earth stick together. He's picturing ___ pouring down on that ground.

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Trust me, this conversation is FAR from over.
